skill.name: changelog-generator

security_audit.summary: No evidence of prompt injection or malicious data exfiltration was found in SKILL.md. Most static command findings are Markdown formatting or safe Git examples; the remaining concern is a documented hook example that uses a predictable temporary file.

remediation.issue: The pre-release hook example writes to /tmp/changes.txt.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique temporary file from mktemp, quote the path, and delete it after use.

remediation.issue: The skill includes Bash examples for collecting Git history.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that users should review commands before running them in hooks or CI.

content.user_title: Generate Release Notes From Git Commits
content.value_statement: Release notes are hard to write from raw commit messages. This skill turns Git history into clear changelog sections for users, teams, and releases.
actual_capabilities: Collects commit history from Git ranges, dates, or recent work.
Groups commits into features, fixes, performance, docs, tests, chores, and breaking changes.
Rewrites technical commit messages into user-facing release notes.
Drafts CHANGELOG.md sections for versioned releases.
Creates GitHub release note summaries with highlights and contributors.
Supports weekly progress summaries for team updates.
limitations: It depends on available Git history and readable commit messages.
It may need human review for customer impact and product naming.
It does not verify whether each commit shipped in a release.
Automation examples should be reviewed before use in CI or hooks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Version Release
use_cases.description: Create a structured changelog from commits since the previous tag.

use_cases.title: Write Product Release Notes
use_cases.description: Convert technical commit messages into short notes that users can understand.

use_cases.title: Summarize Weekly Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Group recent development activity into a concise update for the team.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Release Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple release summary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate release notes from the recent commits. Group changes by feature, fix, docs, and chore.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Changelog Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a versioned changelog entry.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CHANGELOG.md entry for version 1.2.0 using commits since the previous release tag.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for Users
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite these commit messages as user-facing release notes. Keep technical detail only when it affects users.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Notes With Risk Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full release draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate GitHub release notes with highlights, breaking changes, migration notes, contributors, and items that need product review.

output_examples.input: Commits include a new login refresh flow, an order processing fix, and faster dashboard loading.
output_examples.output: New Features: Users stay signed in longer with automatic session refresh. Bug Fixes: Order processing is more reliable. Performance: Dashboard pages load faster.

output_examples.input: A weekly engineering summary is needed for recent commits across docs, tests, and bug fixes.
output_examples.output: This week focused on reliability and maintenance. The team fixed user-reported issues, expanded test coverage, and improved setup documentation.

output_examples.input: A release contains a breaking API route change and several user interface fixes.
output_examples.output: Breaking Changes: API route structure changed and may require client updates. Bug Fixes: Several interface issues were resolved for a smoother user experience.

best_practices: Review generated notes for product accuracy before publishing.
Use consistent commit prefixes so categories stay accurate.
Call out breaking changes with migration guidance.
anti_patterns: Publishing raw commit messages without rewriting them for users.
Hiding breaking changes inside general improvement lists.
Running automation examples in CI without reviewing file paths and permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill write a changelog file?
faq.answer: It can draft or update changelog content when the user asks for that workflow.

faq.question: Does it require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: No, but Conventional Commits help the skill group changes more accurately.

faq.question: Can it create GitHub release notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a format for highlights, all changes, and contributors.

faq.question: Can it summarize a specific date range?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes collecting commits by tag, date, or recent period.

faq.question: Will it know which commits shipped?
faq.answer: Only if the Git history or release range makes that clear.

faq.question: Should generated release notes be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review them for product accuracy, customer impact, and missing context.
